explanation: For the explicit request, T>6 means the first six tests are negative. Thus P(T>6)=(1-9/300)^6=0.97^6=0.832972004929, which rounds to 0.833. The original wording remains ambiguous: counting more than six negative tests before the positive instead gives P(F>6)=0.97^7≈0.808.

reviewed_recovery_request.source_problem: In a medical clinic, a certain rapid test detects a particular infection. On average, $9$ out of every $300$ patients who take the test receive a positive result. Each patient’s test result is independent of the others. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that the nurse will test more than $6$ patients before seeing the first positive result is{{field-1}}.
reviewed_recovery_request.interpreted_problem: In a medical clinic, each patient independently has a probability $9/300$ of receiving a positive rapid-test result. Let $T$ be the total number of patients tested up to and including the first positive result. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability $P(T>6)$ is{{field-1}}.
reviewed_recovery_request.confidence_scope: Only the explicit T>6 request where T includes the first positive; literal before wording remains ambiguous.
